minutes.headline: ZBA voted to deny the water and sewer waivers and signed a stipulation pausing the Pond View Commons 40B hearing for HAC appeal.
minutes.summary: The Zoning Board of Appeals took up a continued 40B comprehensive permit hearing for Pond View Commons, a 200-unit apartment project. Town counsel presented a stipulation to stay proceedings while the water and sewer authority question goes to the Housing Appeals Committee, plus a certificate of partial vote. The board voted on the waivers and the stipulation, with a minimum review period after resumption debated.

public_comment.topic: Asked how the process reached this stage, argued the applicant never submitted a complete application, objected that the applicant was absent, and said the process was being changed to suit the applicant.

votes.motion: Deny waiver two (sewer service) and waiver three (water service) for lack of authority, as set out in the certificate of partial vote
votes.outcome: Roll call by member; captions indicate members voted to deny both, exact count not stated

votes.motion: Accept and sign the stipulation as presented, with a 90-day minimum review period
votes.outcome: passed (members voted aye on roll call; exact count not audible)

votes.motion: Motion to adjourn / close the meeting

budget_items.what_was_said: The hearing was at an impasse because the applicant would not pay for the engineering peer review.
The application fee was not paid in full; the board granted a partial waiver and the partial fee was later paid.
Re-noticing a resumed hearing has a nominal cost borne by the applicant.

Next hearing set for February 22 at 7 p.m. on the 406 Sunset Lane special permit petition.
Board did not seek to change 90 days to 120; it proceeded with the stipulation as negotiated.

what_happened.line: The board voted to deny two waivers, for sewer service and for water service, citing lack of authority, as set out in a certificate of partial vote.
The board voted to accept and sign a stipulation pausing the Pond View Commons 40B hearing while the water and sewer authority question goes to the Housing Appeals Committee.
The stipulation sets a 90-day minimum review period after the hearing resumes; the board debated 90 versus 120 days and kept the negotiated 90.
The certificate of partial vote is to be completed with mover, seconder and vote count, signed, and left with the secretary for filing with the town clerk.
The next hearing was set for February 22 at 7 p.m. on a special permit petition for 406 Sunset Lane.

why_it_matters: The 200-unit Pond View Commons permit is now on hold while the Housing Appeals Committee decides whether the town's water and sewer authority question can be settled, so the project's timing and outcome stay open.
The hearing had been at an impasse over who pays for the engineering peer review, a cost that either the applicant or the town side would otherwise carry.
watch_next: The Housing Appeals Committee's handling of the water and sewer authority question, and the resumption of the Pond View Commons hearing after the stay.
